adopted: field-value violations, codes distinguishable in the reason
consequences: An outcome's code reaches the per-vector reason rather than being collapsed to a boolean, so the four declared failure codes remain distinct observations of distinct causes.

An undeclared code is refused with `amqp:invalid-field` rather than treated as a failure: the code is a declared enumeration, so a value outside it violates the field and does not report an unsuccessful authentication.
`additional-data` on a non-ok code is refused with `amqp:invalid-field`, because the artifact states the field is not set when the authentication is unsuccessful.
The dialogue-level outcome is unchanged: the connection ends either way, so what the reading adds is the reason, not the verdict.
evidence: The outcome's code is declared as a closed set — `ok` beside four failure codes, each naming a distinct cause — and the field carries the artifact's own statement that it is not set on an unsuccessful outcome. The differential contract compares per-vector reason classes and pins named reasons, so a code that reached the outcome and vanished before the report would be a specification that read the field and kept only a boolean. The second citation is carried because the same field-value discipline is what fixes the `sasl-init` mechanism probe: a missing or undeclared value is a violation of the field, not a fault elsewhere in the dialogue.
question: When an outcome carries an undeclared code, or additional-data on an unsuccessful outcome, is that a field-value violation — and does a failure code stay distinguishable once it has been read?

readings.name: field-value violations, codes distinguishable in the reason
readings.statement: Adopted. The code's declared value set is the artifact's, so anything outside it violates the field; and the artifact separates four failure causes, so the reason the peer is told carries which one it was.

readings.name: treat any non-ok code as an indistinguishable failure
readings.statement: Rejected: it reads a declared enumeration and discards what the artifact distinguishes, and it would accept a code the artifact never declared as though the peer had reported something.

readings.name: accept additional-data on an unsuccessful outcome
readings.statement: Rejected: the artifact states the field is not set in exactly that case.
